title: the open deck at 23:40, one sodium lamp
moment: It is 23:40 and I am on the open deck of a night ferry with both hands flat on the wet steel rail. One sodium lamp on the mast, at about 3 o'clock from where I stand, is lighting a fifth of the deck and nothing else; everything past it is black water and a cold wind coming straight at me. The paper boarding pass is folded twice in my coat pocket and I keep checking it is still there. The engines hum up through the soles of my feet, steady, one low note that never changes. I am looking out at nothing, and nothing is looking back.

light.source: one unshaded sodium lamp high on the mast, off to the right
light.fill: a low broken row of very small cold points across the dark, 4000K, faint, never reaching the near surfaces, and one slow cold sweep that passes high above them every few seconds and lands on nothing

objects: wet steel rail, cold grey, running with the lamp's orange spill along its top edge
black water with no horizon in it
the sodium spill lying across one fifth of the painted deck plate
grey non-slip paint worn back to bare metal at the edges
salt haze on everything, softening the one light
a folded paper boarding pass, soft at the crease, warm from the pocket
a damp wool sleeve pushed back off the wrist
inventory.sound: the engines under the feet, one low note that never changes
inventory.text: the sailing time and the fare printed on the folded pass in a thermal dot grid, blunt and slightly smeared
inventory.gesture: both hands flat on the wet rail, holding on
inventory.keepsake: the soft crease where the pass was folded in the pocket all evening
inventory.utterance: We are still an hour out.
